notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.

Statue Park is the most script-driven level in the game: three of its five objectives complete by arriving somewhere and waiting rather than by shooting anything. A bot built only to fight will stall here.

nuance.claim: The objectives fire as a fixed chain rather than in any order the player chooses, so the level is a sequence and not a checklist.
nuance.because: All five objectives share a single minimum difficulty, so the ordering comes from the script rather than from difficulty gating.

nuance.claim: Valentin is contacted by standing in front of him and waiting for the conversation to finish; there is nothing to shoot and leaving early does not complete it.
Janus and his bodyguards do not exist until the player reaches the large statue; the area reads as empty right up until it is not.
The unmasking completes through dialogue after Janus appears, so the objective needs the player to hold position rather than open fire.
The helicopter objective is completed by returning to the level's entrance, so the route doubles back rather than pushing further into the park.
Reaching the unconscious Natalya triggers her escape and the helicopter's destruction, so the two objectives resolve together and neither needs a separate trip.
The flight recorder is thrown back into the park by the explosion, so it does not exist to be collected until the helicopter objective has resolved.
The recorder lands loose in the park rather than at a marked spot, so finding it is a sweep of open ground and not a route to a known point.
The park is open ground broken up by statues and containers that hide guards at close range, so contact tends to come from the flanks rather than ahead.
